key_insight: In liquid-gas coexistence Poiseuille flow, almost all of the pressure drop localizes at the interface, which strongly suppresses the usual bulk momentum-driven particle current.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that multiphase microfluidic and thermal systems can exhibit strong flow resistance and interfacial cooling even under weak driving, so interface effects must be included in design models.
method: Combine Poiseuille flow relations in the liquid and gas bulk regions with Fourier heat conduction.
Enforce particle conservation and energy conservation across the coexistence flow.
Derive small dimensionless parameters A^L and A^G from microscopic-to-macroscopic length-scale ratios.
evidence_signal: The paper’s conclusion is based on analytical bulk equations and scaling arguments, showing that in the weak-driving limit with macroscopic liquid and gas regions the pressure difference concentrates at the interface.
watch_item: The result relies on continuum bulk theory and very small scale-separation parameters, so its applicability may be limited when interface thickness or microscopic effects are not negligible.
paper_title: Pressure-drop localization and momentum insulation in liquid-gas coexistence Poiseuille flow
